record.original_question: (Well-known problem). A finite group G is called an IYB-group if it is isomorphic to the permutation group of a finite involutive non-degenerate set-theoretic solution of the Yang–Baxter equation, or equivalently, G is isomorphic to the multiplicative group of a finite left brace. Assume that the Sylow subgroups of a finite soluble group G are IYB-groups. Is G an IYB-group?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A set-theoretic solution of the Yang–Baxter equation is a pair (X, r), where X is a non-empty set and r : X × X → X × X is a bijection satisfying (r × id)(id × r)(r × id) = (id × r)(r × id)(id × r). Writing r(x, y) = (σ_x(y), τ_y(x)), the solution is called involutive if r∘r = id_{X×X} and non-degenerate if every σ_x and every τ_y is a bijection of X. To each finite involutive non-degenerate solution (X, r) one associates its permutation group, namely the subgroup of Sym(X) generated by {σ_x : x ∈ X}.

Equivalently, a left brace is a triple (B, +, ·) such that (B, +) is an abelian group, (B, ·) is a group, and for all a, b, c ∈ B one has a·(b + c) + a = a·b + a·c. A finite group G is called an IYB-group if it is isomorphic to the permutation group of some finite involutive non-degenerate set-theoretic solution of the Yang–Baxter equation, equivalently if G is isomorphic to the multiplicative group (B, ·) of some finite left brace B.

Question: Let G be a finite soluble group all of whose Sylow subgroups are IYB-groups. Must G itself be an IYB-group?
artifact.status_search_result: The question of whether a finite soluble group whose Sylow subgroups are IYB must itself be IYB is a long-standing open problem. Recent work (2025) establishes partial results — e.g., that every finite soluble group all of whose Sylow subgroups are nilpotent of class at most two is the multiplicative group of a skew left brace, and various positive cases for groups of odd order with structural restrictions on Sylow subgroups — but the general question remains unresolved.

status_evidence.title: New classes of IYB groups
status_evidence.snippet: Every finite group of odd order with all Sylow subgroups of nilpotency class at most two is an IYB group; finite soluble groups with all Sylow subgroups nilpotent of class at most two are multiplicative groups of skew left braces.
status_evidence.claim: Recent partial results address the problem under additional Sylow-structure hypotheses, indicating it is not yet resolved in general.

status_evidence.title: Counterexample to a conjecture about braces
status_evidence.snippet: Discussion of IYB groups and related conjectures on left braces.
status_evidence.claim: The IYB problem for soluble groups with IYB Sylow subgroups continues to be discussed as open in the brace literature.
